reviews.title: My LiveMe Experience: Five Years Later, Nothing Has Changed
reviews.text:
I joined LiveMe over five years ago after being approached by a recruiter as a potential paid host. Although that opportunity didn’t work out, I grew to love the app and its community. However, I experienced what felt like unfair enforcement of its guidelines. I was flagged for wearing shorts or showing my belly button while dancing, yet other streamers could broadcast in bikinis without consequences.

Five years later, I attempted to return, only to find my account still banned with additional allegations, including financial fraud, bullying, and impersonating a host, all of which I strongly dispute. I was simply a comedian and entertainer who danced in wigs, sang, and made people laugh.

I’m sharing this review to warn potential streamers about the unfair bias I believe still exists on this platform. My LiveMe experience was once about love, support, and laughter. It’s disappointing that this is how it ended. There are other platforms worth exploring.

reviews.title: Community
reviews.text:
The app itself works fine. My problem isn’t with the developers—it’s with the community.

First live I joined, I got kicked for asking a simple question. Second live, I followed the host, joined the conversation, and got kicked again because apparently they “didn’t want me around.” What did I do? Nothing. No trolling, no drama, no disrespect. Just normal conversation.

That’s one hell of a first impression. If this is how people treat newcomers, don’t expect users to stick around for long.

To be fair, the developers can’t control every person using the app, so I don’t blame them or the app itself. The issue is the people. Maybe I just had terrible luck. Maybe I’m somehow the most unwanted person in LiveMe. Either way, the experience was bad enough that I have zero interest in staying.

Not a great start.
